key_insight: Commercial AI chatbots vary widely in how accurately they report emerging news: retrieval and synthesis integration—especially across regions and languages—is a primary source of error and inconsistency.
problem_solved: Provides the first systematic, multi-model, multi-region measurement of how commercial chatbots handle same-day emerging facts, revealing where and why they fail as news intermediaries.
method: 14-day live evaluation (Feb 9–22, 2026) of six commercial chatbots: Gemini 3 Flash & Pro, Grok 4, Claude 4.5 Sonnet, GPT-5, and GPT-4o mini.
2,100 factual questions derived from same-day BBC News across six regions/languages to probe timeliness, factuality, attribution, and cross-lingual consistency.
Quantitative scoring and qualitative analysis of retrieval-synthesis behavior to identify common failure modes (misattribution, hallucination, stale retrievals).
impact: Equips AI/ML practitioners and product teams with evidence about real-world risks when using chatbots as news intermediaries, guiding improvements in retrieval, attribution, and deployment safeguards.
visual_elements: Bar chart comparing per-model factual accuracy and attribution rates
Heatmap showing performance by region and language to highlight geographic blind spots
Timeline/flow diagram of the retrieval→synthesis pipeline with annotated common failure modes
Icon-driven summary panel listing top error types (hallucination, misattribution, stale data)
paper_title: Evaluating Commercial AI Chatbots as News Intermediaries
paper_authors: Mirac Suzgun, Emily Shen, Federico Bianchi, Alexander Spangher, Thomas Icard
